Ref: Search public and private documentation and read pages as markdown while using as few tokens as possible.
By Ref. Docs & Knowledge.
Listing page: https://mcp.tc/i/ref-tools
Server URL (connect to this): https://api.ref.tools/mcp
Access: Needs an API key from Ref, sent in the X-Ref-Api-Key header.
Ref gives coding agents access to documentation for APIs, services and libraries. It searches public docs on the web and GitHub, plus private sources such as repos and PDFs, and reads a URL as markdown. It uses the MCP session's search history to skip repeated results and return only the most relevant part of a page, about 5k tokens. A hosted streamable HTTP endpoint is available at https://api.ref.tools/mcp, which takes an API key in the X-Ref-Api-Key header or an apiKey query parameter. A…
Setup (call get_server with client=<id> for the full steps):
- Claude Code (claude-code): `claude mcp add --transport http ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>"`
- Claude Desktop (claude-desktop): see client=claude-desktop
- claude.ai (claude-ai): Add to claude.ai: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Ref&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.ref.tools%2Fmcp
- Cursor (cursor): Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=ref-tools&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5yZWYudG9vbHMvbWNwIiwiaGVhZGVycyI6eyJYLVJlZi1BcGktS2V5IjoiPFlPVVJfQVBJX0tFWT4ifX0%3D
- VS Code (vscode): see client=vscode
- Devin Desktop (devin): see client=devin
- Codex (codex): `codex mcp add ref-tools --url https://api.ref.tools/mcp`
- Gemini CLI (gemini): `gemini mcp add --transport http --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp`
- Any client (json): see client=json

structuredContent.name: Ref
structuredContent.tagline: Search public and private documentation and read pages as markdown while using as few tokens as possible.
structuredContent.description: Ref gives coding agents access to documentation for APIs, services and libraries. It searches public docs on the web and GitHub, plus private sources such as repos and PDFs, and reads a URL as markdown. It uses the MCP session's search history to skip repeated results and return only the most relevant part of a page, about 5k tokens. A hosted streamable HTTP endpoint is available at https://api.ref.tools/mcp, which takes an API key in the X-Ref-Api-Key header or an apiKey query parameter. A local stdio package, ref-tools-mcp, runs with npx and reads REF_API_KEY. The source is MIT licensed.
structuredContent.auth_note: Needs an API key from Ref, sent in the X-Ref-Api-Key header.

capabilities: Search public documentation on the web and GitHub
Read any URL converted to markdown
Skip repeated results across similar searches in a session
Return the most relevant part of a long page
Expose search and fetch tool names for OpenAI deep research
example_prompts: Find the Figma REST API endpoint for posting a comment.
Search the docs for how the n8n Merge node handles multiple inputs.
Read this documentation URL and summarize the auth section.
Look up the correct usage of this library's config options in its docs.

setup.label: Claude Code
steps: Run this in a terminal, in your project folder:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>"
```
Replace the placeholder with your key before you run it, then check it with `/mcp` inside Claude Code.
setup.code: claude mcp add --transport http ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>"
setup.note: Add `--scope user` to make it available in every project, not just this one.

setup.label: Claude Desktop
steps: Use the `mcp-remote` bridge, which keeps the key on this computer (a connector added on claude.ai with the key under **Request headers** also shows up here). Open **Settings → Developer → Edit Config** and add:
Replace the placeholder with your key and restart Claude Desktop.
setup.note: The bridge needs Node.js on your computer.

setup.label: claude.ai
steps: Open the connector form on claude.ai. This button fills in the name and URL for you:
Add to claude.ai: https://claude.ai/customize/connectors?modal=add-custom-connector&connectorName=Ref&connectorUrl=https%3A%2F%2Fapi.ref.tools%2Fmcp
Check that the URL reads `https://api.ref.tools/mcp`. Under **Request headers**, add `X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>` with your key from Ref, then click **Add**.
Turn it on in a chat from the tools menu.
setup.note: Free plans allow one custom connector. On Team and Enterprise plans an owner adds it under **Organization settings → Connectors**.

setup.label: Cursor
steps: Add to Cursor: https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=ref-tools&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5yZWYudG9vbHMvbWNwIiwiaGVhZGVycyI6eyJYLVJlZi1BcGktS2V5IjoiPFlPVVJfQVBJX0tFWT4ifX0%3D
Or add it by hand to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (all projects) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (this project):

setup.label: VS Code
steps: Add it to `.vscode/mcp.json`. VS Code asks for the key the first time and stores it securely:

setup.label: Devin Desktop
steps: Add it to `~/.config/devin/mcp_config.json` (macOS and Linux) or `%APPDATA%\devin\mcp_config.json` (Windows):
Refresh the MCP server list in Cascade.
setup.note: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf. It reads `serverUrl` (or `url`) for remote servers.

setup.label: Codex
steps:
```bash
codex mcp add ref-tools --url https://api.ref.tools/mcp
```
Or edit `~/.codex/config.toml` directly:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ref-tools]
url = "https://api.ref.tools/mcp"
env_http_headers = { "X-Ref-Api-Key" = "X_REF_API_KEY" }
```
setup.note: Codex reads the header values from the environment variables named in `env_http_headers`.

setup.label: Gemini CLI
steps:
```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp
```
setup.code: gemini mcp add --transport http --header "X-Ref-Api-Key: <YOUR_API_KEY>" ref-tools https://api.ref.tools/mcp
setup.note: This adds it to the current project. Add `-s user` to use it everywhere.

setup.label: Any client
steps: Most clients accept this shape. Some name the URL field differently: `serverUrl` in Devin Desktop, `httpUrl` in Gemini CLI’s settings file.
Zed puts servers under `context_servers` in its settings. Cline needs `"type": "streamableHttp"`, or it assumes SSE.
Client only starts local servers? Bridge it with `npx -y mcp-remote https://api.ref.tools/mcp`.
